How this server is labelled in the app.

That is normal for a server that still uses the certificate it created for itself. Before you continue, compare the fingerprint below with the one shown on the server. If they match, the connection is to your server.

The certificate is different from the one you trusted before. This happens when a certificate is renewed or replaced, and also when something is intercepting the connection. Continue only if the fingerprint below matches the one shown on the server.
On the server, open the node, then System, then Certificates. The fingerprint is listed there.
Your password isn\'t stored. You\'ll sign in again after the app has been closed.

Enter your user name and password.
Enter the full token ID, such as root@pam!phone, and its secret.

No server was found at that address. Check the spelling and your network connection.
The server didn\'t respond. Check the address and port, and that this device is on a network that can reach it.
A secure connection couldn\'t be set up.
The server presented a different certificate again. Check the new fingerprint below.
This account signs in with a security key. Choose Browser to sign in on the server\'s own page.
This account uses a second factor the app can\'t ask for. Choose Browser to sign in on the server\'s own page.
Couldn\'t refresh. Showing the last data received.

The virtual machine restarts at once without shutting down. Unsaved data inside it may be lost.

Only needed when a reverse proxy in front of the server asks for them. Header values are stored encrypted.
A header has a name or value that can\'t be sent. Names use letters, digits and dashes; values use plain ASCII.
The client certificate is no longer available. Choose it again.
The password is stored encrypted on this device. The app uses it to sign in again by itself. Accounts with a second factor still ask for the code.
Sign in on the server\'s own page, inside the app. Use this for security keys and single sign-on. The app takes over the session when you\'re done and keeps nothing else from the page.
This server offers single sign-on, which works only this way.
Security keys work on the page only if the server\'s domain allows this app. Otherwise, sign in with a password and a code, or an API token.
The sign-in page stopped working. Try again.
The page didn\'t produce a usable session. Try again.
Shown while consoles stay connected in the background.
The row of keys above the keyboard in the terminal. Arrows, Page Up, Page Down and Delete repeat while held.
No extra keys. The row is hidden.
%1$d sp. Pinching the terminal changes it too.
Bundled under the SIL Open Font License 1.1
Touch mode: the pointer goes where you touch. Switch to trackpad mode.
Trackpad mode: drag to move the pointer. Switch to touch mode.

Tap to click, long-press or tap with two fingers to right-click, drag with two fingers to scroll, double-tap and drag to drag, and pinch to zoom.\n\nThe display has no sound. Its resolution is set inside the guest and doesn\'t follow this screen. The clipboard is shared only when the virtual machine\'s display has the VNC clipboard switched on and the guest runs the SPICE guest tools.
No snapshots yet. A snapshot keeps the guest\'s disks as they are now, so you can go back to them.
Include memory, so a rollback resumes the running machine
Starts with a letter. Letters, digits, - and _ only.
The guest\'s disks return to the snapshot. Everything changed since is lost. A running guest is stopped first.
You can\'t roll back to it afterwards. The guest itself is not changed.
No backups of this guest on the storages this node can reach.
This node has no storage for backups.
The guest keeps running. Fastest, with the least interruption.
The guest is paused briefly for a consistent copy.
The guest is shut down for the backup and started again after. Most consistent.
The guest\'s disks and settings are replaced by the backup\'s. Everything changed since it was taken is lost.
Shut the guest down first. A running guest can\'t be restored over.
The virtual machine keeps running while it moves.
The container is restarted on the new node.
The guest is stopped, so it moves at once.
No other online node can take this guest.
This guest uses devices tied to its node, so it can\'t move: %1$s
Copy the local disks %1$s to the new node
Copy every disk (a full clone). A linked clone shares the template\'s disks.
A template can\'t be started, only cloned. This can\'t be undone.
The guest and its disks are deleted for good. Backups are kept.
Shut the guest down first. A running guest can\'t be deleted.
Also remove it from backup jobs, replication and high availability
Choose one of the listed values.

Settings saved. Some apply after the guest restarts.

Enter a whole number from %1$d to %2$d.
How many cores\' worth of time the container may use. Empty or 0 means no limit.
The guest can give back memory down to this amount. 0 turns ballooning off.
Use a value no higher than the memory.
This bus has no free slot. Choose another.
No storage on this node can hold disks.
Disks can only grow. The guest\'s partitions and file systems must be grown inside it too.
The disk is kept as an unused disk, so it can be attached again or destroyed later.
The disk and everything on it are deleted. This cannot be undone.
The drive is removed from the guest. The ISO image stays on its storage.
The guest has as many network devices as it can take.
The guest loses this network connection.
Use letters, digits, hyphens and dots, not starting or ending with a hyphen.
Windows needs UEFI and a TPM, so both are added. Its installer needs VirtIO drivers to see a SCSI disk.
No ISO images on this node. The guest starts with an empty drive.
A small disk for UEFI settings is added on the same storage.
Start it once it is created
Give a password of at least 5 characters, an SSH key, or both.
Allow nesting, which systemd in newer distributions needs

Leave empty to use the node\'s DNS settings.
Guests on this node shut down or migrate as configured, and the node starts again. Its consoles and remote desktops disconnect.

The node could not do this.
All packages are up to date.
Whatever depends on this service stops working until it is started again.
Changes take effect when you apply the configuration.
A mistake can cut the node off from the network, including from this app.
The interface goes once the configuration is applied. Guests attached to it lose their connection.
Interface removed. Apply the configuration to take effect.
The file is removed from the storage. This cannot be undone.
The file could not be deleted.
The file\'s name does not fit this kind of content. ISO images end in .iso or .img, templates in .tar.gz, .tar.xz or .tar.zst.

No backup jobs. Guests are not backed up on a schedule.

Its guests are no longer backed up on its schedule. Backups it already made stay.
Backups started. Follow them in Tasks.

Servers are checked when the phone has a network. A server signed in with a password is checked only if its password is saved and it needs no second factor; API tokens always work. Android may check less often to save battery.
